explanations.3: This tells the system to not ask interactive questions during package installation—just proceed silently, which is necessary in containers where nobody can answer prompts.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the package cache files to shrink the image size, since we won't need them again.
explanations.14: This runs the Oh-My-Zsh installer script by downloading it from the internet and piping it directly to the shell, a common but slightly unusual pattern.
explanations.20: The `sed` command finds the line starting with `plugins=(git)` and replaces it with a version that also includes the zsh-autosuggestions plugin.
explanations.24: The `printf` command writes multiple lines into the shell history file so that when you start the container and press up-arrow, you'll see previous commands ready to autocomplete.
explanations.33: The `-i` flag makes the shell interactive (so it shows a prompt), and `-l` makes it a login shell (so it reads your startup files like .zshrc).
